Block 4 Data Summary: Half-Hourly FLUXNET Observations Across Five Ecosystems

Author: Sanglap Roy (Student 22)
Data source & versions: FLUXNET Shuttle snapshot fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261116T075027.csv, ONEFlux processing v1.3_r1 (_FLUXMET_HH_ half-hourly archives in data/raw/, downloaded 16 November 2026).
Methods & variable choices: - Missing values (-9999) are read as NaN via scripts/read_flux.py (read_hh()). - Timestamps (TIMESTAMP_START) are parsed from text to datetime64 in local standard time (no daylight-saving jump). - Carbon fluxes use the variable-u*-threshold reference product (_VUT_REF) with night-time partitioning (GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF) and quality flag NEE_VUT_REF_QC (0 = measured, > 0 = gap-filled). - Meteorology (TA_F, SW_IN_F, VPD_F, P_F) and energy fluxes (NETRAD, G_F_MDS, H_F_MDS, LE_F_MDS) use gap-filled (_F / _F_MDS) series, with H_F_MDS_QC == 0 and LE_F_MDS_QC == 0 selecting measured turbulent fluxes for energy-balance closure.

Snapshot file: fluxnet_shuttle_snapshot_20261116T075027.csv
Archive files: ['AMF_US-Vcm_FLUXNET_2007-2025_v1.3_r1.zip', 'EUF_NL-Vkp_FLUXNET_2014-2025_v1.3_r1.zip', 'ICOS_BE-Lon_FLUXNET_2004-2024_v1.3_r1.zip', 'JPF_ID-PaD_FLUXNET_2001-2017_v1.3_r1.zip', 'TERN_AU-How_FLUXNET_2002-2025_v1.3_r1.zip']
Loaded 1,630,512 half-hourly rows across 5 sites (duplicates: 0).

C2. Data Coverage

Best overall site: NL-Vkp (41.6% mean); highest single year: AU-How 2019 (50.9%).

Coverage note: AU-How, NL-Vkp, and BE-Lon have the best overall measured NEE coverage (~41.5%–41.6% of all half-hours), with the single highest-coverage years occurring at AU-How in 2019 (50.9%), BE-Lon in 2015 (50.6%) and 2020 (50.4%), and AU-How in 2017 (50.5%) and 2023 (50.1%); ID-PaD has the lowest overall measured NEE share (19.4%, with 15.1% completely missing and <7% measured in 2001, 2008, and 2009). ## C3. C6. Your Reading

Synthesis & Comparison

Across the five towers, the tropical woody savanna AU-How takes up the most carbon per year (−730.1 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹), followed by the Belgian cropland BE-Lon (−347.1 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹), the Indonesian peatland forest ID-PaD (−236.8 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹), the subalpine conifer forest US-Vcm (−96.9 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹), and the Dutch grassland NL-Vkp (−47.3 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹). BE-Lon exhibits the largest seasonal cycle in monthly mean NEE (6.24 µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹ amplitude between summer crop uptake and winter respiration), whereas US-Vcm has the smallest seasonal amplitude (1.62 µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹) and lowest productivity (GPP = 587.3 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) at ~3,000 m elevation. Several patterns were surprising: NL-Vkp is nearly carbon-neutral despite high photosynthesis (GPP = 1,820.5 vs RECO = 1,784.3 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹), ID-PaD lacks all night-time partitioned GPP_NT_VUT_REF and RECO_NT_VUT_REF values (100% -9999 in v1.3_r1, though _DT_ values exist), and AU-How shows remarkably strong net NEE uptake (noting that periodic savanna fire losses are not captured by eddy covariance). At AU-How, half-hourly energy balance closure against NETRAD − G yields a linear slope of 0.819 (R² = 0.887, n = 254,495), reflecting the typical ~18% energy imbalance of eddy covariance measurements. Finally, a large share of every record relies on gap-filling (NEE_VUT_REF_QC > 0): 55.1% at AU-How, 56.2% at NL-Vkp, 56.5% at BE-Lon, 65.5% (plus 15.1% missing) at ID-PaD, and 74.9% (22.6% measured) at US-Vcm. ## Data and Citation
